#image("/imgs/ap-calc-ab-2009-frq-06-diagram-01.png", width: 65%)

The derivative of a function $f$ is defined by $f'(x)= lr(\{ mat(delim: #none, g(x) "", " for " "", - 4 <= x <= 0 ""; 5 e^(- x \/ 3)- 3 "", " for " "", 0 < x <= 4))$. The graph of the continuous function $f'$, shown in the figure above, has $x$-intercepts at $x = - 2$ and $x = 3 ln lr((frac(5,3)))$. The graph of $g$ on $- 4 <= x <= 0$ is a semicircle, and $f(0)= 5$.

(a) For $- 4 < x < 4$, find all values of $x$ at which the graph of $f$ has a point of inflection. Justify your answer.

(b) Find $f(- 4)$ and $f(4)$.

(c) For $- 4 <= x <= 4$, find the value of $x$ at which $f$ has an absolute maximum. Justify your answer.
